710747.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pró, from Proto-Indo-European *pró, *pro- (see *per-). Cognates include Latin pro, Sanskrit प्र- (prá-), Proto-Celtic *ɸro and Proto-Germanic *fram (English from).

710771.t: From Proto-Hellenic *prógʷlāmə. Equivalent to προβάλλω (probállō, “to throw before”) + -μα (-mă).

710712.t: From πρᾶγμα (prâgma, “a thing done, a fact”) + -ικός (-ikós).

710729.t: From πρεσβεύω (presbeúō, “to be elderly; to be ambassador”) + -εία (-eía, “nominal suffix”) and see πρέσβυς (présbus, “elder”).

710706.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kʷosyo. Compare its indefinite form πού (poú), as well as πόθεν (póthen).

710783.t: From προδίδωμι (prodídōmi, “to betray”) + -της (-tēs, masculine agent-noun suffix).

710721.t: From Proto-Hellenic *prā́t͏̌t͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *pr̥h₂-k-yé-ti, a *k-enlargement of *per- (“to go over, cross”).

710708.t: From πράσσω (prā́ssō, “I do, practice”) + -μα (-mă, result noun suffix).

710705.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kʷís. Compare its interrogative form ποῦ (poû).

710735.t: From πρέσβυς (présbŭs, “aged”, “elder”) + -τερος (-teros, suffix forming comparative degrees of adjectives).

710733.t: The first component of the word is likely from Proto-Indo-European *pres (“before, in front”), an extended form of *per-.

710742.t: Appears to be related to πρό (pró), Latin prior, priscus and Lithuanian prie, but the exact formation is uncertain. Perhaps from an old locative *pr-i of Proto-Indo-European *pró (“forward”).

710720.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *pr̥so- (“leek”), and connected with Latin porrum (“leek”) and Albanian presh.

710751.t: From προαιρέομαι (proairéomai) + -σις (-sis). From προ- (pro-) + αἵρεσις (haíresis, “taking; choice”).

710743.t: According to Beekes, from a substrate root common to Proto-Slavic *brinъ (“larch”).

710746.t: Etymology tree Ancient Greek πρίω (príō) Proto-Indo-European *-ō Ancient Greek -ων (-ōn) Ancient Greek πρίων From πρίω (príō, “to saw, to cut”) + -ων (-ōn).

710745.t: Likely from Proto-Hellenic *príhō. This element is also found in Mycenaean Greek *𐀠𐀪𐀁𐀳 (*pi-ri-e-te /⁠prihentēr⁠/).

710702.t: Nominalization of the neuter of ποτός (potós, “drinkable, for drinking”), from Proto-Indo-European *ph₃tós, from *peh₃- (“to drink”).

710782.t: From the verbal stem of προδίδωμι (prodídōmi, “to betray”) (προ-, the preposition, and -δω-, the verbal stem of δίδωμι) and the suffix -σια (-sia) (a suffix often used in nouns derived from verbs or adjectives) From προ- (pro-) and δίδωμι (dídōmi, “to…

710704.t: A zero-grade nominal form from Proto-Indo-European *peh₃- (“to drink”), though the exact derivation is unclear.

710703.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ph₃tós (“(having been) drunk”). Cognate with Latin pōtus and Sanskrit पी॒त (pītá).

710738.t: Perhaps from Proto-Hellenic *prḗtʰō, from Proto-Indo-European *préh₁-dʰe-ti, from *preh₁-.
